title: Finite free evaluation over an affine direct-image algebra is epi iff surjective on affine sections
statement: Let $f:U\to X$ be an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and put $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_U$ and $\mathcal N=f_*\mathcal F$, with $\mathcal A(T)=\mathcal O_U(f^{-1}T)$ acting on $\mathcal N(T)=\mathcal F(f^{-1}T)$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $V\subseteq X$ be an affine open and $I$ a finite set. For compatible sections $s_i$ of $\mathcal N|_V$, let $\phi:\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal A|_V\to\mathcal N|_V$ be the $\mathcal A|_V$-linear map sending its $i$th basis section to $s_i$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. Then $\phi$ is an epimorphism of sheaves of modules if and only if $\phi_V:\mathcal A(V)^I\to\mathcal N(V)$ is surjective. No finite-type assumption on $\mathcal N$ or $\mathcal F$ is made.

source.place: Tag 0897 (coherent-lemma-graded-finiteness), proof, omitted finite-type detail; Tag 01SB (morphisms-lemma-affine-equivalence-modules), affine-local equivalence; Tag 01IC, exactness of tilde and quasi-coherent images. This is the finite-free evaluation argument of steps 2 and 3 of lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-finite-type.

proof.text: Restrict scalars along O_X -> f_* O_U on the over-site of V and transport with Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V to O_V-modules. This functor T changes no underlying abelian sheaf under scalar restriction. Its action on morphisms preserves and reflects epimorphisms: the faithful forgetful functors to abelian sheaves preserve epimorphisms, and their maps of the same morphism are definitionally identical. The over-site equivalence also preserves and reflects epimorphisms. At the top open of V, the corresponding over-site object is Over.mk(id_V), giving exactly the sections map in the statement. These comparisons are proved explicitly by epi_restrictScalars_iff and the terminal-object calculation in Lean.

The transported target is the restriction to V of the ordinary O_X-module f_*F. It is quasi-coherent by affine pushforward quasi-coherence and restriction along an open immersion. Likewise the transported unit A|V is the restriction of f_*O_U and is quasi-coherent. T is additive by the componentwise formula for its map, so Mathlib preservesFiniteCoproductsOfAdditive and PreservesCoproduct.iso identify the transported finite free source with the finite coproduct of its transported units. Coproducts of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent; therefore source and target of T(phi) are quasi-coherent. The finite coproduct comparison uses the given Finite I instance, including the empty case.

If phi is epi, so is psi=T(phi). Its abelian image inclusion is then an isomorphism; hence its map on global sections of V is surjective. Apply the affine image formula in quasiCoherent_cokernel_image to identify the range of this inclusion on the top affine open of V with the range of psi. Thus psi is surjective on global sections, and the top-open comparison gives the required surjectivity for phi.

Conversely, surjectivity of phi at Over.mk(id_V) is surjectivity of psi on the top open of V. The one-member affine cover {top} covers the affine scheme V. Apply epi_of_surjective_app to psi, whose target is quasi-coherent, and that cover to get Epi psi. Reflection of epimorphisms by the scalar-restriction and over-site transport gives Epi phi.

proof_origin.place: J1 scalar-restriction proof of the finite-free affine evaluation argument of Tags 01SB and 01IC: affine pushforward quasi-coherence, finite coproduct closure, affine image formula, and the affine-cover epimorphism criterion. The over-site and scalar-restriction comparisons are proved explicitly in Lean.
